subject: Post-call recap: AcmeHealth private VPC / air-gapped requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-22T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call recap: AcmeHealth private VPC / air-gapped requirements

Hi Samir

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we all have the same picture. Please correct me if I missed anything.

Key pain points / drivers:
- Regulatory: need to keep PHI on-prem or in a customer-managed VPC.
- Network restrictions: strict egress controls and no public internet access from inference hosts (air-gap preferred for certain workflows).
- Auditing: detailed audit logs and customer-managed KMS/HSM for key material are required.
- Latency predictability for real-time triage workflows is important (SLO: p95 < 250ms).

What we discussed as potential Redwood approaches:
- Private deployment inside AcmeHealth VPC with dedicated GPU nodes and controlled egress.
- Option for an air-gapped on-prem bundle if networking restrictions cannot be relaxed.
- Integration with Acme KMS/HSM (we support KMIP and cloud KMS integrations).
- Audit and retention: configurable logging and retention policies; we can export logs to your SIEM.

Open / requested items from AcmeHealth:
1) Network diagram (to understand NAT/firewall/proxy topology).
2) List of allowed outbound endpoints/ports or the policy team contact for a presales network call.
3) Clarify whether full air-gap is required for all traffic or only for model download/updates.

Attachments: redwood-private-overview.pdf (high-level architecture + presales checklist).

Next steps:
- Rajesh: share network diagram and any existing firewall rules (Rajesh, can you share by EOD Wednesday?).
- Dev: schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra/networking team (30-45m).
- Marissa / Stephanie: we will follow up with a tailored SOW template and an initial estimate for capacity and timeline.

Thanks

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: AcmeHealth private VPC / air-gapped requirements

Marissa

Thanks for the summary, that matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side:

- We do need customer-managed keys (FIPS 140-2 level) for production.
- For now, model downloads and updates must happen over an approved staging network; production inference hosts must not have outbound internet access (air-gap).
- We can share a network diagram and firewall rules; I'll loop in Rajesh (network lead) to share the diagram and a point of contact for a networking call.

Rajesh

Can you share the current network topology and any proxy/NAT constraints? Preferably by Thursday EOD.

Also, pricing/contract: our procurement team will need an outline SOW and security questionnaire (SOC2, GDPR data processing addendum). Can Redwood provide a SOC2 letter and a short SOW example we can review?

Thanks,
Samir
Director of Clinical Systems | AcmeHealth

Thanks Samir / Rajesh

Got the diagram, Rajesh. Quick technical notes after a first pass:

- For air-gapped inference hosts we typically provide an offline installer (signed artifacts) plus a small bootstrap that your network team can validate. Model weights and runtime images can be transferred via an approved staging network or swing media depending on your policy.
- We will need the following details to prepare the presales runbook:
  * Allowed ports between the control plane (if any) and the inference cluster, or confirmation that the control plane will be fully customer-hosted.
  * Whether DNS resolution is allowed outbound or must be internal only.
  * KMS/HSM endpoint details (we can support KMIP and several HSM vendors).

Proposed next step: 45-minute technical deep-dive next week with your networking and security engineers. Suggested times: Tue 2/24 10:00-10:45 PT or Wed 2/25 13:00-13:45 PT. Which works best for you?

I'll also attach a short presales checklist and a sample SOW for an on-prem/private deployment in the follow-up.

Cheers,
